questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to **abandon**.
questions.explanation: To abandon is to leave or give up for good.

questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to **generous**.
questions.explanation: Generous means giving freely; stingy means unwilling to give.

questions.question: One word for "a long speech by one person":
questions.explanation: A monologue is spoken by one person. A dialogue is between two.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to **frugal**.
questions.explanation: Frugal means thrifty and economical.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to **inevitable**.
questions.explanation: Inevitable means impossible to avoid.

questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to **optimistic**.
questions.explanation: An optimist expects good outcomes; a pessimist expects bad ones.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Each of the employees ___ a badge.
questions.explanation: "Each" is singular: has.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: She is afraid ___ dogs.
questions.explanation: The usual phrase is "afraid of".

questions.question: Fill in the blank: He ___ in this office for ten years.
questions.explanation: "For ten years" with a situation that continues up to now needs the present perfect.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: I wish I ___ more time.
questions.explanation: "Wish" about the present takes the past form: had.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Not only the students but also the teacher ___ late.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the nearer subject, "teacher" (singular).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The furniture in the office ___ new.
questions.explanation: "Furniture" is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: He avoided ___ the question.
questions.explanation: "Avoid" is followed by a gerund (-ing form).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The movie was ___ boring that we left early.
questions.explanation: "So + adjective + that" shows result.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Definitely comes from "finite": def-i-nite-ly.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Privilege has no d and ends in -lege.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Calendar ends in -dar.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Environment keeps the n before the m: environ-ment.

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: The manager is signing the letters.
options: The letters are being signed by the manager.
The letters were signed by the manager.
The letters are signed by the manager.
The letters have been signed by the manager.
questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes "are being + past participle".

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: Who wrote this report?
options: By whom was this report written?
By whom this report was written?
questions.explanation: A "who" question in the passive is "By whom was ... written?".

questions.question: Change to the active voice: The room was cleaned by the staff.
options: The staff has cleaned the room.
The staff were cleaning the room.
questions.explanation: Simple past stays simple past.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: He said, "I have finished the work."
options: He said that he had finished the work.
He said that he has finished the work.
He said that I had finished the work.
He said that he will finish the work.
questions.explanation: Present perfect shifts back to past perfect.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: She asked me, "Do you know him?"
options: She asked me that do I know him.
She asked me if I knew him.
She asked me did I know him.
She asked me if do I know him.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with "if" or "whether", in statement order.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **to break the ice**.
options: to start a conversation in an awkward situation
questions.explanation: It means to ease tension at the start of a meeting.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **to call it a day**.
options: to stop working for the day
to wait for a long time
questions.explanation: It means to stop what you are doing for now.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **under the weather**.
questions.explanation: It means feeling unwell.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **the ball is in your court**.
options: it is your turn to act
questions.explanation: The next move or decision is yours.

questions.question: The "Ref. No." on an office letter is used for:
questions.explanation: A reference number identifies the letter in the office file.

questions.question: The agenda of a meeting is:
options: a record of what was decided
the date of the next meeting
a list of items to be discussed
questions.explanation: The agenda is prepared before the meeting.

questions.question: The minutes of a meeting are:
options: the time limit for each speaker
a written record of what was discussed and decided
a list of items to be discussed
questions.explanation: Minutes are prepared after the meeting.

questions.question: In an email, "FYI" means:
questions.explanation: FYI is used when sharing something that needs no action.

questions.passage:
**Read the passage and answer the next 3 questions.**
Linux is a family of operating systems built around the Linux kernel. The kernel manages the processor, memory and devices, while the rest of the system is supplied by distributions such as Ubuntu or Fedora. Because the source code is open, anyone may study and improve it. Most web servers and supercomputers run Linux, partly because it is stable and can be configured without paying for licences.
questions.question: What does the kernel manage, according to the passage?
questions.explanation: The second sentence says the kernel manages the processor, memory and devices.

Notice: The annual maintenance of the electrical system will be carried out on Saturday from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. Power will be unavailable in the laboratory block during this time. Staff are requested to shut down their computers on Friday evening and not leave any experiment running.
questions.question: What is the staff asked to do on Friday evening?
questions.explanation: The notice asks staff to shut down computers and not leave any experiment running.

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. As a result, the match was postponed.
Q. Heavy rain fell throughout the morning.
R. The ground became too wet to play on.
S. It will now be played next Sunday.
questions.explanation: Rain (Q), wet ground (R), result (P), new date (S).

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. Then she sent it to her manager for approval.
Q. Meena wrote the report on the audit.
R. She checked every figure twice.
S. The final version was filed on Friday.
questions.explanation: Write (Q), check (R), send for approval (P), file (S).

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. The next day, the team found the cause.
Q. The website went down at midnight.
R. Engineers worked through the night to restore it.
S. A faulty plug-in had been installed earlier.
questions.explanation: Outage (Q), night work (R), next day cause found (P), the cause explained (S).

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. They are then collected by the van and taken to the city.
Q. Farmers pick the vegetables early in the morning.
R. The vegetables are packed in crates at the village.
S. By noon they are on sale in the market.
questions.explanation: Pick (Q), pack (R), collect and carry (P), sell (S).
